CITY COUNCIL MEETING - NOVEMBER 16, 2026 
 
1 
The Portland City Council will hold a City Council Meeting in Council Chambers.  The Honorable Mark 
Dion, Mayor, will preside. 
 
To submit written public comment on an agenda item, email publiccomment@portlandmaine.gov. Submissions 
must be received by 12:00 pm the day before the Council meeting to guarantee their inclusion in the agenda 
packet. All submissions must include the commenter's name and legal address. To help ensure your comment is 
submitted for the correct item, please include the order number (see below). 
 
The City Council will conduct this meeting from Council Chambers, located on the second floor of City Hall.

ANNUAL MEETING: 
  
 Annual Meeting of the Corporator of the Creative Portland Corporation 
    
  
Pursuant to the Bylaws of Creative Portland (CP), the Portland City Council, as 
Corporator of Creative Portland, shall hold its annual meeting in the month of November 
each year or at a special meeting.  This year's Annual Meeting Agenda includes: 
 
1.  Accepting CP FY 2026 Activity and Financial Reports; and, 
2.  Transaction of other business as may be deemed necessary. 
 
In addition to Creative Portland's signature program,  the First Friday Art Walk, notable 
contributions in FY2026 included: 
 
1.  Creative Portland Marketing Wheel:  A Monthly Arts Update Newsletter is published 
on the first of each month with over a 70% open rate (3,000).  By the Summer of 2026, 
the cultural tourism initiative attracted 5,700 downloads total to the Creative Portland 
app, and 63,000 active users (in one year) to the website that includes a free artist
2 
directory, self-guided tours, and lists of galleries, museums, music clubs, and cultural 
events. 
 
2.  Monday Morning Drop By Program - an open house for arts community stakeholders 
on the first Monday morning of each month (attracts 12 to 30 participants each month). 
 
3.  Creative Portland Art Gallery - "Resistance", their 9th juried arts exhibition, features 
14 local artists work for sale.  Opened on May 1, 2026. 
 
4.  Hear Here 3 - a live local performing arts showcase at Merrill Auditorium on 
September 7, 2025 (600 attendees, one-third benefiting from free community passes). 
 
5.  The 6th Biennial Portland Arts & Culture Summit on September 22, 2026 (FY27 Q1) 
at the University of Southern Maine. 
 
6.  Artist Activation Program - Open Call and plans for an Arts District Flagpole Banner 
refresh for August 2025, in collaboration with the Portland Museum of Art to include 
wayfinding for cultural organizations. 
 
7.  Fiscal Sponsorship Program including 82 Parris, Maine Music Festival & Arts in 
Greenwood. 
 
8.  Third Wednesdays - an art activation program in the 500 Congress Street block of the 
Arts District from June to October 2026. 
 
This item requires no public comment or formal Council action.

APPOINTMENTS: 
  
 Order 80-26/27 Appointing Phillip Cruess as a Constable for the Portland Police 
Department - Sponsored by Danielle P. West, City Manager 
    
  
This order appoints Phillip Cruess, an employee of the Police Department, as a constable 
pursuant to Chapter 20, Sections 20-19 and 20-19.5 of the Portland City Code. Constables 
are authorized to enforce specific municipal regulations and issue civil notices of 
violation. Constables are not sworn law enforcement officers, have no authority to make 
arrests, and are prohibited from carrying firearms, concealed or unconcealed, in the 
performance of their duties. 
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment.

RESOLUTIONS: 
  
 Resolve 6-26/27 Approving the Reimagining Franklin Street Plan and Planning 
Study - Sponsored by Sustainability & Transportation Committee, Councilor 
Regina Phillips, Chair 
    
  
On October 21, 2026, the Sustainability and Transportation Committee voted 
unanimously (3–0) to forward the Reimagining Franklin Street Plan to the City Council 
for consideration. The project originated from City Council direction in 2024, when the 
Council unanimously authorized the City to enter into a Village Partnership Initiative 
(VPI) agreement with the Maine Department of Transportation (MaineDOT) (Order 119-
23/24) to undertake a planning study for the Franklin Street corridor. The study’s purpose 
is to finalize a transportation design and land use concept that advances a more 
multimodal, complete street with improved connectivity, bicycle and pedestrian facilities, 
and an enhanced streetscape, while creating opportunities for new development, 
particularly housing, and the expansion of Lincoln Park. 
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment.
4 
 Resolve 7-26/27 Recommending Tariff Amendment to Prohibit Open-Loop Exhaust 
Gas Cleaning System (Scrubber) Discharges at City-Owned Marine Terminals - 
Sponsored by Councilor Regina Phillips & Councilor Pious Ali 
    
  
This resolution requests that the City Manager amend City of Portland Terminal Tariff 
No. 11 to prohibit commercial vessels from operating open-loop exhaust gas cleaning 
systems (scrubbers) or discharging scrubber wash water while berthed at city-owned 
marine terminals, specifically the Portland Ocean Terminal and Ocean Gateway 
Terminal, to protect Portland’s coastal waters and ecosystem from preventable chemical 
and particulate contamination. 
 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
UNFINISHED BUSINESS: 
  
 
Order 78-26/27 Accepting and Appropriating and Additional $74,572.50 from the 
Land and Water Conservation Fund and Approving the Amendment to the Sub-
Grant Between Portland and the Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation & 
Forestry RE: Riverton Trolley Park Improvements - Sponsored by Danielle P. West, 
City Manager 
    
  
This item requests authorization to accept and appropriate an additional $74,572.50 in 
grant funding from the Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) for ongoing 
improvements at Riverton Trolley Park. These supplemental funds will supplement the 
initial project allocation and support the continued enhancement of park infrastructure, 
recreation features, and public access. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on November 2. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
 
Order 79-26/27 Amending the Conditional Zone Agreement RE: Second 
Amendment to the Conditional Rezoning Agreement for Property in the Vicinity of 
St. Lawrence Arts/Congress Street - Sponsored by the Planning Board, Joseph 
Zamboni, Chair 
    
  
On October 27, 2026, the Planning Board held a public hearing and voted 6-0 (Messina 
absent) to recommend that the City Council adopt Hill Arts’ (“Applicant”) proposed 
amendments to Conditional Zoning Agreement C-58 for 76 Congress Street, with one 
modification: to further amend the proposal to include a 10-year time limit from the date 
of execution to the date of receiving a Certificate of Occupancy permit. The Board found 
that the amendments are consistent with the Comprehensive Plan for the City of Portland. 
As submitted, the amendments would allow minor modifications to the previously 
approved development, replacing the Parish Hall theater, reducing the overall proposal to 
a single 424-seat auditorium, and eliminating the agreement’s expiration date. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. It received its first reading on November 2. 
Five affirmative votes are required for passage after public comment. 
    
ORDERS: 
  
 Order 84-26/27 Accepting and Appropriating a $20,000 Maine Emergency 
Management Agency Grant - Sponsored by Danielle P. West, City Manager
5 
  
This order authorizes the acceptance of $20,000 in funding from the Fiscal Year 2025 
Homeland Security Grant Program. This funding will be used to enhance preparedness 
and response capabilities for homeland security incidents. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. To meet the grant deadline for acceptance, 
staff is requesting that the second reading be waived, which requires seven affirmative 
votes. Staff also requests that this item be passed as an emergency. Seven votes are 
required for passage as an emergency following public comment. 
    
 
Order 85-26/27 Approving Modification 1 to Locally Administered Project 
Agreement Between the Maine Department of Transportation and Portland for 
Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Improvements on West Commercial Street - 
Sponsored by Danielle P. West, City Manager 
    
  
This project is part of MaineDOT’s Locally Administered Project (LAP) Program. 
TheCity of Portland DPW will administer the project and pays 10 percent of the 
estimated cost. The modification increases the project amount from $170,783 to 
$300,000. By signing the modified partnership agreement, it enables MaineDOT and 
DPW to proceed with the project and obligates the City to pay for 10% of the modified 
estimated project cost; the City share for this initial phase of design work is estimated to 
be $30,000, an increase of $12,921.70 from the original City estimated City share of 
$17,078.30. The MaineDOT, using state and federal funding, will be paying $270,000. 
 
This item must be read on two separate days. To allow this project to begin before winter 
weather, staff is requesting that the second reading be waived, which requires seven 
affirmative votes. Staff also requests that this item be passed as an emergency. Seven 
votes are required for passage as an emergency following public comment.
